full_judgment:
2. The short facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.1-12, namely, Hakimuddin as the pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.29 of 1994 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for pre-emption of the Case land described in the schedule to the application for pre-emption. The case of the pre-emptor, in short, was that he is a co-sharer tenant by inheritance of the case holding. The case land originally belonged to CS recorded tenants Nizamuddin and Leju in equal share. Leju died Leaving behind two sons, Fajar Ali and Fajila and one daughter Anesa as his heirs. Fazila died leaving one son Hakimuddin, (the pre-emptor) and one daughter Khatun Bibi. SA khatian had been prepared in their names. Subsequently, Fajar Ali died leaving respondent Nos. 13-16 and one daughter Sukur Banu. Leju's daughter transferred her share before her death. By this way, Hakimuddin became co-sharer of the case holding. After sale of their land in 1984, pre-emptees did not have any interest in the case holding. On 7-3-1999, vendor-respondent Nos. 13-16, secretly sold the case land to the pre-emptee- appellants. On 3-3-1994, pre-emptee No. 1 disclosed about the fact of their purchase of the case- land to the pre-emptor. On 13-4-1994, the pre-emptor got definite knowledge of sale by obtaining certified copy of the deed of sale and filed application for pre-emption. On 28-4-1951, Shaharjan Bibi obtained decree in Title Suit No. 90 of 1948 for partition of the case land and some other lands. Leju's daughter Anesa Bibi was defendant No. 3 in that suit who got her saham from plot Nos. 177 and 182 and she did not get any land from plot No. 180. 

 3. Pre-emptee-appellants contested the case by filing written objection denying the material statements made in the application for pre-emption. Their case, in short, was that Leju and Nizamuddin were CS recorded owners of the land of plot No. 180 appertaining to khatian No. 172 and some other lands. CS recorded tenant Leju was owner of 0.25 acre of plot No. 180 and his brother Nizamuddin was owner of 0.121/2 acre of land, Leju died leaving behind two sons Fajar Ali and Fajita and one daughter Anesa. Thereafter, Anesa died leaving behind one son HaSan Ali and one daughter Fatema Begum and predeceased daughter Matia Begum's two sons, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-2. Getting 0.01-7/8 acre of land in plot No. 180 by inheritance, they have been possessing the same. Nizamuddin's daughter Shaharjan Obtained decree on 25-2-1953 in Title Suit No. 90 of 1948 for partition and in the said suit Fajar Ali got 0.25 acre of land from plot No. 180. Respondent Nos. 13 to 16 are the heirs of Fajar Ali, who sold their shares to the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 within the knowledge of the pre-emptor on 7-3-1994. The pre-emptee Nos. 1-2 got some lands from Anesa Bibi by a deed of gift which were recorded in their names. Since the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 are co-sharers of the case holding, the present application for pre-emption of the case land against them is not maintainable. Thus, the pre-emptor is not entitled to get the order of pre-emption of the case land. 

 7. Admittedly, the land of the disputed CS khatian originally belonged to Nizamuddin and Leju. Leju died leaving two sons Fajar Ali and Fajila and one daughter Anesa. Pre-emptor is the son of Fazila who had another daughter named Khatun Bibi. SA record of right also prepared in their names. It is the case of the pre-emptees that Leju's daughter Anesa died leaving one son Hasan Ali and daughter Fatema Begum and sons of another daughter Motia. The pre-emptees are the heirs of Motia. It is the claim of the pre-emptor that the pre-emptees are not the co-sharers of the case holding since their predecessor transferred her share elsewhere. The pre-emptor produced exhibit-6 and 6(Ka) and tried to prove that the share of Anesa was transferred elsewhere. From the judgment and decree of the Courts of facts it appears that both the courts, considering exhibit 8, certified copy of the decree of the partition suit No. 90 of 1948, found that Anesa got 0.69 acres of land from plot No. 182 and 177. Aforesaid Exhibits show that Anesa sold .331 acre of land from plot No. 182 and, after her transfer, she had 0.3534 acre of land more in plot No.182 of the disputed holding. 

 8. Since Anesa got 0.3534 acre of land in plot No. 182 and SA khatian shows that pre-emptor and Anesa both are the recorded tenants and co-sharers of the case holding, the finding of the High Court Division that Anesa Bibi and her successive heirs, the pre-emptees ceased the co-shareship of the case holding is erroneous. Such conclusion arrived at by the High Court Division is not based upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record.
